entry: Combined military forces of [[North Korea]] and the armed wing of the [[Workers' Party of Korea]]. It has five branches: the Ground Force, Naval Force, Air Force, Strategic Force and Special Operations Forces. It is commanded by the Central Military Commission and by the president of State Affairs; [[Kim Jong Un]] heads both posts. Its primary adversaries have been the Republic of Korea Armed Forces and United States Forces Korea since the Armistice Agreement of July 1953. As of 2021 it is the second-largest military organization in the world, with 29.9% of the North Korean population serving in it or in reserve or paramilitary roles.

Armed conflict on the Korean Peninsula, fought from June 25, 1950, to July 27, 1953, between [[North Korea]] and [[South Korea]] and their allies. North Korea, backed by China and the [[Soviet Union]], invaded the South in June 1950. A [[United Nations]] force under a unified command, led by the [[United States]], supported South Korea, and the United States provided around 90% of its military personnel. After UN forces landed at Inchon on September 15, they recaptured Seoul and advanced into North Korea until Chinese forces entered the war that October. Fighting then became a war of attrition near the 38th parallel. The Korean Armistice Agreement, signed July 27, 1953, created a Demilitarized Zone along the front line. The war caused around one million military deaths and an estimated 1.5 million to 3 million civilian deaths. No peace treaty has been signed.

Koreanic language native to Korea and the official language of both [[North Korea]] and [[South Korea]]. It is spoken by about 81 million people, most of them in Korea. Outside the peninsula it is a minority language in parts of China and among Sakhalin Koreans in Russia. The closely related language of [[Jeju Island]] is not mutually intelligible with it. [[Sejong the Great|King Sejong the Great]] developed the alphabetic [[Hangul]] script in the 15th century to promote literacy among common people, but [[Chinese characters]] (Hanja) remained the primary script until the mid-20th century. Hangul uses 24 basic letters (jamo) and 27 complex letters formed from them. Korean is ranked at the top difficulty level for English speakers by the United States Department of Defense.

Body of [[Myth|myths]] told by historical and modern Koreans, in two main forms. Literary mythology, recorded in traditional Hanja histories such as *Samguk sagi* and *Samguk yusa*, consists mostly of state-foundation myths about the founders of ancient kingdoms. The best known is that of Gojoseon and its legendary king Dangun, which became the founding myth of the whole Korean nation. Oral mythology is much larger and more varied. It consists of shamanic narratives sung by *mansin* (shamans or priestesses) in rituals that invoke the gods, and is revised with each performance. These narratives are often at odds with official ideologies and are frequently characterized as subversive of patriarchy. The mythology of southern [[Jeju Island]] is especially divergent. Two narratives, *Jeseok bon-puri* and *Princess Bari*, appear in nearly all regions. In the latter, a princess abandoned by her father revives her dead parents with the flower of life.

American [[Nu metal|nu metal]] band from [[Bakersfield, California]]. Formed in 1993 by James Shaffer, Reginald Arvizu and David Silveria, it is credited with pioneering the genre. Its debut album, *Korn*, appeared in 1994, and *Follow the Leader* (1998) and *Issues* (1999) both debuted at number one on the *Billboard* 200. As of 2021 the band had sold more than 40 million records worldwide. It has won two [[Grammy Awards]] from eight nominations.

Landlocked country in Southeastern Europe, with partial diplomatic recognition and its capital at [[Pristina]]. It covers 10,887 sq km (4,203 sq mi) and borders [[Albania]] to the southwest, [[Montenegro]] to the west, [[Serbia]] to the north and east, and [[North Macedonia]] to the southeast. About 92% of its population are ethnic Albanians. Kosovo was part of the [[Ottoman Empire]] for nearly five centuries until 1912, after which it was ceded to the Kingdom of Serbia. After World War II it became an autonomous province within Yugoslavia. Kosovo declared independence from Serbia on February 17, 2008. Serbia does not recognize it as a sovereign state and continues to claim it as an autonomous province. In December 2022 Kosovo applied for membership in the [[European Union]].

Armed conflict in [[Kosovo]] from February 28, 1998, to June 11, 1999, between Federal Republic of Yugoslavia forces and the Kosovo Albanian militia known as the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA). The KLA had been formed to fight the discrimination of ethnic Albanians and the repression of political dissent by Serbian authorities. [[NATO]] began an air campaign in March 1999, and Yugoslav forces withdrew under the Kumanovo Agreement. The bombing caused at least 488 Yugoslav civilian deaths and remains controversial. Over 13,500 people were killed or went missing during the war, and between 1.2 million and 1.45 million Kosovo Albanians were displaced.

Former ungoverned Chinese enclave in [[British Hong Kong]]. Originally a military fort, it remained under Chinese claim after the New Territories were leased to Britain in 1898. After World War II refugees swelled its population, and by 1987 it had an estimated 33,000 residents in 2.6 hectares. From the 1950s to the 1970s local triads controlled it, and it became a center of [[Prostitution|prostitution]] and [[Gambling|gambling]]. In 1984 Britain and China agreed to demolish it, and demolition took place between 1993 and 1994. Its unusual architecture has inspired many works of [[Cyberpunk|cyberpunk]] fiction.

Language family of mainland Southeast Asia, southern China and northeastern India, also known as Tai–Kadai or Daic. About 93 million people speak Kra–Dai languages, 60% of them Thai, and Ethnologue lists 95 languages in the family. All are tonal, including Thai and Lao, the national languages of [[Thailand]] and [[Laos]]. Weera Ostapirat proposed the name Kra–Dai in 2000, replacing Tai–Kadai, whose two-branch classification is now considered obsolete. James R. Chamberlain proposes that the family formed as early as the 12th century BCE in the middle [[Yangtze]] basin. Whether it is related to the [[Austronesian languages]] remains contested.

German electronic band formed in [[Düsseldorf]] in 1970 by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider. Kraftwerk began within [[West Germany]]'s experimental krautrock scene before adopting synthesizers, drum machines and vocoders. Albums such as *Autobahn* (1974), *Trans-Europe Express* (1977), *The Man-Machine* (1978) and *Computer World* (1981) developed a "robot pop" style that combined electronic music with pop melodies. The band influenced synth-pop, [[Hip-hop|hip-hop]], post-punk, techno and house music. It received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2014 and was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2021. Hütter continued to lead the band after Schneider left in 2008.

City in southern Poland on the [[Vistula]] River, second-largest in the country (pop., 2025: 816,614). It was the official capital of Poland until 1596. The city began as a fortified settlement on Wawel Hill around the 8th century. From 1038 it was the seat of Polish monarchs of the Piast dynasty, and it remained a center of the [[Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]] until [[Sigismund III Vasa]] moved the royal court to [[Warsaw]] in the late 16th century. Its Old Town was declared a [[World Heritage Site]] in 1978, one of the first in the world. After the [[Invasion of Poland]], the city became the seat of Nazi Germany's General Government, and its Jewish population was confined to a [[Ghetto]] before deportation to camps such as Auschwitz. Jagiellonian University, one of the oldest in the world, is located here.

Volcanic caldera in the Sunda Strait between [[Java]] and [[Sumatra]], [[Indonesia]]. The eruption of August 26–27, 1883, created the caldera and destroyed two-thirds of the island of Krakatoa. With an estimated volcanic explosivity index of 6, it was equivalent to 200 megatons of TNT and was among the most violent volcanic events in recorded history. The explosion was heard 3,600 km away in [[Alice Springs]], Australia. At least 36,417 people died, mostly from [[Tsunami|tsunamis]] that followed the explosion. Anak Krakatau ("Child of Krakatoa") emerged from the caldera in 1927. A major collapse in 2018 triggered a tsunami. The name probably derives from a [[Sanskrit]] word for lobster or crab.

Legendary sea monster of enormous size, said to appear in the [[Norwegian Sea]] off [[Norway]]. The legend may have originated from sightings of [[Giant squid|giant squid]]. The kraken was first described in a Norwegian glossary in 1646. In 1753 the Danish bishop Pontoppidan described it as an [[Octopus|octopus]] of tremendous size that pulled down ships. [[Victor Hugo]] identified it with the pieuvre of [[Guernsey]] lore in his 1866 novel *Toilers of the Sea*, and [[Jules Verne]] depicted it in *Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas*. The word derives from Norwegian *kraken*, a form of *krake*, meaning a malformed or overgrown tree.

Horned figure from Central and Eastern Alpine folklore who accompanies [[Saint Nicholas]] on visits to children on the night of December 5. Saint Nicholas rewards well-behaved children with small gifts, while Krampus punishes badly behaved ones with [[Birch|birch]] rods. Its origin is unclear. Historians consider a pre-Christian origin unlikely, because the figure is not attested until the 16th century. Young men dressed as Krampus scare spectators in traditional parades and in events such as the *Krampuslauf*. The figure has appeared in films, TV shows and video games around the world.

Israeli self-defense system developed for the [[Israel Defense Forces]]. Imi Lichtenfeld, a Hungarian-born martial artist who grew up in [[Bratislava]], developed it from his training in [[Boxing|boxing]] and [[Wrestling|wrestling]]. He used these skills to defend Jewish neighborhoods in the mid-to-late 1930s, and after his move to [[Mandatory Palestine]] he taught the Jewish paramilitary groups that later formed the IDF. The name means "contact combat" in Hebrew. The system stresses aggression and simultaneous defensive and offensive moves, and it targets the most vulnerable parts of the body. Civilian versions are taught internationally.

Identical twin criminals who led an organized crime network in East London. Ronald and Reginald Kray, born in Haggerston, ran a gang known as the Firm from Bethnal Green from the late 1950s. Its activities included murder, armed [[Robbery|robbery]], arson, protection rackets, [[Gambling|gambling]] and assaults. In the 1960s the twins mixed with prominent members of [[London]] society. They were arrested in May 1968, and in 1969 each was sentenced to [[Life imprisonment|life imprisonment]].

Fortified complex in central [[Moscow]], Russia. The Moscow Kremlin, the best known of the many kremlins in Russian cities, comprises five palaces, four cathedrals, an enclosing wall and numerous towers. Its Grand Kremlin Palace was a royal residence of the tsars and is now the residence of the president of the Russian Federation. Dmitri Donskoi replaced an earlier oak palisade with a white limestone citadel in 1366–68. The walls as they now appear were built between 1485 and 1495. Saint Basil's Cathedral was constructed beside the complex during the reign of [[Ivan the Terrible]]. During the [[Cold War]], "the Kremlin" meant the government of the [[Soviet Union]]. The complex was designated a [[World Heritage Site]] in 1990, along with Red Square.

Small, shrimp-like marine [[Crustacean|crustaceans]] of the order Euphausiacea, found in all the world's oceans. Krill feed mainly on phytoplankton and are a key link near the bottom of the food chain. The Antarctic krill makes up an estimated biomass of around 379 million tonnes, and over half of that biomass is eaten each year by whales, seals, [[Penguin|penguins]], [[Seabird|seabirds]], squid and fish. Krill are the main food of baleen whales, including the [[Blue whale]]. The total global harvest of 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes a year is used mainly for [[Aquaculture|aquaculture]] and [[Aquarium|aquarium]] feeds, bait and human consumption. The name comes from the Norwegian word for "small fry of fish".

American musician, songwriter and actor. A pioneer of the outlaw [[Country music|country]] movement of the 1970s, he wrote hits including "For the Good Times", "Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down" and "Me and Bobby McGee" (1970). Born in [[Brownsville, Texas]], he enlisted in the military in the early 1960s before signing with Monument Records in 1969. He made his film debut in *The Last Movie* (1971) and worked with director Sam Peckinpah on *Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid* (1973). He was a member of the country supergroup the Highwaymen from 1985 to 1995. He received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2014.

River in southern India, third-longest in the country after the Ganga and Godavari. It rises in the [[Western Ghats]] near Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra, at about 1,300 metres, and flows about 1,400 km (870 mi) east to the [[Bay of Bengal]]. It passes through Maharashtra, [[Karnataka]], [[Telangana]] and [[Andhra Pradesh]]. Its basin covers 258,948 sq km, nearly 8% of India's geographic area, and is the fifth-largest river basin in the country. The river is a major source of [[Irrigation|irrigation]] in these states. Principal tributaries include the Bhima, Tungabhadra and Malaprabha rivers. The Krishna-Godavari delta is known as the "Rice Granary of India".

Major deity in [[Hinduism]], worshipped as the eighth [[Avatar|avatar]] of [[Vishnu]]. His name means "black" or "dark", and he is often depicted with dark skin. Krishna is a central figure in the [[Mahabharata]] and the [[Bhagavad Gita]], where as Arjuna's charioteer he delivers philosophical teachings. He was born in Mathura and raised in Gokul, and he later defeated the tyrant Kamsa. In some sub-traditions he is worshipped as the Supreme God. His worship spread to the Western world from the 1960s, largely through ISKCON. Krishna's birthday is celebrated as Krishna Janmashtami in late August or early September of the [[Gregorian calendar]].

Emperor of the [[Vijayanagara Empire]] (r. 1509–1529) and third ruler of the Tuluva dynasty. Widely regarded as one of the greatest rulers in Indian history, he presided over the empire's political and cultural zenith. He became the dominant ruler of the Indian peninsula by defeating the sultans of Bijapur, Golconda and the Bahmani Sultanate, and the Gajapatis of [[Odisha]]. Major campaigns included the conquest of the Raichur Doab in 1512, the subjugation of Odisha in 1514 and a decisive victory over the sultan of Bijapur in 1520. Portuguese travelers Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa described him as an able administrator and an exceptional military commander. His reign is regarded as a golden age of Telugu literature, and he composed the Telugu poem *Amuktamalyada*.

[[Pogrom]] against Jews across [[Nazi Germany]] on November 9–10, 1938. Carried out by the [[Schutzstaffel|SS]] and SA, with participation from the Hitler Youth and civilians, it destroyed over 1,400 [[Synagogue|synagogues]] and prayer rooms and damaged or destroyed more than 7,000 Jewish businesses. Around 30,000 Jewish men were arrested and sent to concentration camps. The pretext was the shooting of German diplomat Ernst vom Rath in Paris by Herschel Grynszpan, a 17-year-old Polish Jew. Early reports estimated that 91 Jews were murdered, but modern estimates put the total at between one and two thousand. Historians regard the pogrom as a prelude to the [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]].

American actress and director. Born and raised in [[Los Angeles]], she achieved international stardom as Bella Swan in *The Twilight Saga*, five films released yearly from 2008 to 2012 that collectively grossed over $3.3 billion worldwide. Her independent roles include *Clouds of Sils Maria* (2014) and *Personal Shopper* (2016). She received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for playing [[Diana, Princess of Wales]] in *Spencer* (2021). Her film debut as a director, *The Chronology of Water*, premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.

Khan of the [[First Bulgarian Empire]] (r. 803–814), often called Krum the Fearsome. During his reign the Bulgarian territory roughly doubled, spreading from the middle [[Danube]] to the [[Dnieper]] and from Odrin to the Tatra Mountains. In 809 he forced the surrender of Serdica, and in 811 his forces trapped the retreating army of [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] emperor Nikephoros I in the Varbitsa Pass, killing the emperor. It is said that Krum had the emperor's skull lined with silver and used it as a drinking cup. His rule brought law and order to Bulgaria and developed the rudiments of state organization.
